.  In the academic discourse, this is referred to as ‘acquiescent immobility’: people who are immobile, and content to be so. In the Pacific, in particular, the desire to remain in place is now a key touchstone. When New Zealand offered a ‘climate’ visa in 2017, it was shelved due to lack of interest; the new climate-related pathway offered by Australia has attracted opprobrium in Tuvalu.
